symbols.name: Oobs
symbols.role: observed part of one sampled experimental unit

symbols.name: Fobs
symbols.role: information available to the planner after observing row \(n\)

symbols.name: Pn
symbols.role: row law under a local alternative

symbols.name: Delta
symbols.role: causal reward contrasts relative to action \(0\)

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: \(\mathcal H\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a supplied nonempty rational hyperrectangle

symbols.name: muhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\mu_{n,ja}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_{ni}=j,A_{ni}=a\}Y_{ni}}{\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_{ni}=j,A_{ni}=a\}}\) when the denominator is positive and \(0\) otherwise

symbols.name: V
symbols.role: generic covariance in the declared envelope

symbols.name: lambdan
symbols.role: vanishing KL weight in outcome units

symbols.name: pistar
symbols.role: oracle Gibbs lottery at the local penalty

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: For \(c=t/(1-t)\) and \(0<t<1\), \(G(u,z)(t)=(1+c)\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j\ell_{c,b_j}(Ru_j,Rz_j)\); \(G(u,z)(0)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j[\max_{a\in\mathcal A}(Ru_j)_a-(Ru_j)^{\top}q_{0,b_j}\{R(u_j+z_j)\}]\); and \(G(u,z)(1)=\frac12\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_jz_j^{\top}R^{\top}C(b_j)Rz_j\)

symbols.name: Tn
symbols.role: oracle normalized causal-regret path that is the covered target

symbols.name: Front
symbols.def: For \(c=t/(1-t)\) and \(0<t<1\), \(\mathfrak F_{r,b}(v)(t)=(1+c)\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}r_j[\Psi_{c,b_j}(Rv_j)-b_j^{\top}Rv_j]\); at \(t=0\), it equals \(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}r_j[\max_{a\in\mathcal A}(Rv_j)_a-b_j^{\top}Rv_j]\); and at \(t=1\), it equals \(\frac12\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}r_jv_j^{\top}R^{\top}C(b_j)Rv_j\)
symbols.role: compactified welfare-gain frontier computable at supplied weights and contrasts

symbols.name: Fhat
symbols.role: sample-computable plug-in welfare frontier used for temperature selection

symbols.name: dBL
symbols.def: \(d_{\mathrm{BL}}\) is the bounded-Lipschitz metric induced by the bounded version of the ambient norm

symbols.name: wcap
symbols.role: maximum number of adaptive subdivision nodes before the analytic fallback

symbols.name: epsbar
symbols.def: \(\overline\varepsilon_n\in\mathbb Q_+\) is a supplied directed-rounding upper bound satisfying \(\overline\varepsilon_n\ge\varepsilon_n\)
symbols.role: machine-readable upper certificate for the path approximation error

symbols.name: Bgamma
symbols.role: Gaussian coordinate-truncation radius used by the guaranteed fallback

symbols.name: mA
symbols.role: maximum requested precision of every interval oracle

symbols.name: Bup
symbols.def: \(B_\gamma^+\in\mathbb Q\) is the outward-rounded upper endpoint for \(B_\gamma\) returned at precision \(m_{\mathsf A}\)
symbols.role: rational truncation radius recorded in the fallback certificate

symbols.name: Nops
symbols.role: explicit upper bound on certified box operations and interval-oracle calls

symbols.name: IO
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak O=(\mathfrak o_p,\mathfrak o_b,\mathfrak o_-,\mathfrak o_+,\mathfrak o_{p,0},\mathfrak o_{b,0},\mathfrak o_\varepsilon)\) returns componentwise outward rational intervals for \(p\), \(b\), \(v_{\min}\), \(v_{\max}\), \(p_{\min}\), \(\beta\), and \(\varepsilon_n\)
symbols.role: effective names for nonrational numerical inputs

symbols.name: InputRep
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak R=(n,J,K,\alpha,\gamma,\zeta,w_{\max},\mathcal H,\overline\varepsilon_n,\mathfrak O)\), where \(\mathcal H\) has rational endpoints and, on every query \(m\in\mathbb N\), each component of \(\mathfrak O\) returns an outward rational interval of width at most \(2^{-m}\); a rational symmetric-matrix box covers \(\mathcal K_V\), boxes certified disjoint from its spectral inequalities are discarded, and every undecided box is retained as an outer box for the optimization over \(V\)
symbols.role: finite names for all data, envelopes, and optimized parameters used by calibration

symbols.name: Eledger
symbols.role: separate certified discretization and probability errors

symbols.name: Cert
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak C=(q^+,\mathcal E_n,\mathcal P_t,\mathcal P_h,\mathcal P_V,\mathcal P_z,\mathcal I_G,\mathcal I_\phi,L_{\mathrm{CDF}},B_\gamma^+,\mathsf{branch})\), where \(q^+\), \(B_\gamma^+\), and every partition endpoint are rational, \(L_{\mathrm{CDF}}\) is a rational lower bound, and \(\mathsf{branch}\in\{\mathsf{refined},\mathsf{fallback}\}\)
symbols.role: portable certificate verified by rational inequalities and directed interval enclosures

symbols.name: Alg
symbols.sig: \(\mathsf A(\mathfrak R)=(q^+,\mathcal E_n,\mathfrak C)\in\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q_+^6\times\mathsf{Cert}\)
symbols.def: From the effective record \(\mathfrak R\), perform at most \(w_{\max}\) best-first rational subdivisions of the temperature, local-contrast, covariance, and truncated Gaussian boxes. Evaluate \(G\), the Gaussian density, and every elementary transcendental with outward directed rounding; accept a refined value only when its rational lower-CDF sum verifies the target. Otherwise output the rational analytic fallback \(q^+=2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\), whose certificate uses \(S(h,z)\le2\|z\|_\infty+\|z\|_\infty^2/2\) and the union Gaussian-tail bound.

symbols.name: Qplus
symbols.def: \(Q^+_{n,\alpha}\) is the critical-value output of \(\mathsf A(\mathfrak R)\) at Gaussian target probability \(1-\alpha+\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}\)

symbols.name: Calpha
symbols.role: inflated simultaneous critical value for the oracle regret path

symbols.name: that
symbols.def: \(\widehat t_n\) is any \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable map into \([0,1]\); in particular it may be any Borel-measurable functional of \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\)

symbols.name: AChandle
symbols.def: The handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{AC}}\) stratifies Gaussian contrast space by benchmark-weighted hard maximizing sets, covers the smooth temperature interior by a finite net, and applies coarea or Gaussian polynomial small-ball bounds on each stratum while charging decision-boundary slabs separately.
symbols.role: starting move for the open anti-concentration problem

symbols.name: Mclass
symbols.type: class of triangular arrays of laws

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(P_n\).
\(\max_{a\in\mathcal A}|Y(a)|\le B_Y\) almost surely under every \(P_n\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)=\{(P_n)_{n\ge1}:\text{conditions }\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}rows},\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:randomization},\mathrm{ass:stratum\mbox{-}mass},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:bounded\mbox{-}outcomes},\mathrm{ass:local\mbox{-}remainder},\mathrm{ass:benchmark\mbox{-}support},\mathrm{ass:covariance\mbox{-}envelope}\text{ hold}\}\)

definitions.name: \(\widehat\Delta_n\)
definitions.construction: Compute each nonempty randomized cell mean \(\widehat\mu_{n,ja}\), set it to \(0\) only on the empty-cell event, and stack \(\widehat\mu_{n,ja}-\widehat\mu_{n,j0}\) over \(j\in\mathcal J\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\setminus\{0\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}=\sigma\{(X_{ni},A_{ni},Y_{ni}):1\le i\le n\}\). It excludes \(Y_{ni}(a)\) for \(a\ne A_{ni}\), the row law \(P_n\), the true contrast \(\Delta_n\), the local state \(u_n\), and the estimation error \(E_n\).

definitions.name: \(q_{c,b}\)
definitions.construction: \(q_{c,b}(v)_a=b_a\exp(v_a/c)\big/\sum_{r\in\mathcal A}b_r\exp(v_r/c)\).

definitions.name: \(\Psi_{c,b}\)
definitions.construction: \(\Psi_{c,b}(v)=c\log\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}b_a\exp(v_a/c)\).

definitions.name: \(\ell_{c,b}\)
definitions.construction: \(\ell_{c,b}(u,z)=\Psi_{c,b}(u)-\Psi_{c,b}(u+z)+z^{\top}q_{c,b}(u+z)\).

definitions.name: \(W_{n,\lambda}\)
definitions.construction: \(W_{n,\lambda}(\pi)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\mu_{n,ja}\pi_{ja}-\lambda\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi_j\|b_j)]\).

definitions.name: \((\pi^*_{n,c},\widehat\pi_{n,c})\)
definitions.construction: \(\pi^*_{n,c,j}=q_{c,b_j}(Ru_{n,j})\) and \(\widehat\pi_{n,c,j}=q_{c,b_j}(R\widehat u_{n,j})\), where \(\widehat u_n=\sqrt n\,\widehat\Delta_n=u_n+E_n\). The learned lottery is therefore \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable although its oracle comparator is not observed.

definitions.name: \(\mathscr R_n(c)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr R_n(c)=W_{n,\lambda_n(c)}(\pi^*_{n,c})-W_{n,\lambda_n(c)}(\widehat\pi_{n,c})\).

definitions.name: \(q_{0,b}\)
definitions.construction: \(q_{0,b}(v)_a=b_a\mathbf 1\{a\in I(v)\}\big/\sum_{r\in I(v)}b_r\).

definitions.name: \(\ell_{0,b}\)
definitions.construction: \(\ell_{0,b}(u,z)=\max_{a\in\mathcal A}u_a-u^{\top}q_{0,b}(u+z)\).

definitions.name: \(G(u,z)\)
definitions.construction: Use \((1+c)\sum_jp_j\ell_{c,b_j}(Ru_j,Rz_j)\) for \(c=t/(1-t)\) on \(0<t<1\), the benchmark-weighted hard-argmax formula at \(t=0\), and \(\frac12\sum_jp_jz_j^{\top}R^{\top}C(b_j)Rz_j\) at \(t=1\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\)
definitions.construction: Set \(\widehat p_{n,j}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_{ni}=j\}\) and \(\widehat u_n=\sqrt n\,\widehat\Delta_n\). For \(c=t/(1-t)\) and \(0<t<1\), define \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n(t)=(1+c)\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\widehat p_{n,j}[\Psi_{c,b_j}(R\widehat u_{n,j})-b_j^{\top}R\widehat u_{n,j}]\). Define \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n(0)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\widehat p_{n,j}[\max_{a\in\mathcal A}(R\widehat u_{n,j})_a-b_j^{\top}R\widehat u_{n,j}]\) and \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n(1)=\frac12\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\widehat p_{n,j}\widehat u_{n,j}^{\top}R^{\top}C(b_j)R\widehat u_{n,j}\).

definitions.name: oracle normalized regret path \(T_n\)
definitions.construction: \(T_n=G(u_n,E_n)\). This is the causal target path covered by the band; it is not presented to the planner as an observed plug-in path.

definitions.name: \(\widehat t_n\)
definitions.construction: Choose any \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable map into \([0,1]\). A frontier-based choice is obtained by applying any Borel-measurable functional on \(C([0,1])\) to the observed path \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\).

definitions.name: \(\varepsilon_n\)
definitions.construction: \(\varepsilon_n=C_{\mathrm{map}}\inf_{M\ge1,\ 0<a\le1/4,\ x_n\le a/8}[\sqrt{r_n}+JK^2a/\sqrt{v_{\min}}+d\exp\{-M^2/(2v_{\max})\}+Ma+x_n(1+M)^2\log\{\exp(1)+M/a\}/a]\).

definitions.name: \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\)
definitions.construction: \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}=\inf\{q\in\mathbb R:\inf_{h\in\mathcal H,V\in\mathcal K_V}P[S(h,Z_V)\le q]\ge1-\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak R\)
definitions.construction: Supply binary encodings of \(n,J,K,w_{\max}\), rational \(\alpha,\gamma,\zeta,\overline\varepsilon_n\), and the rational endpoints of \(\mathcal H\). Supply \(\mathfrak O\) as seven total interval oracles which, for every integer \(m\ge0\), halt with outward rational intervals of width at most \(2^{-m}\) containing the coordinates of \(p\), the coordinates of \(b\), \(v_{\min}\), \(v_{\max}\), \(p_{\min}\), \(\beta\), and the displayed computable bound \(\varepsilon_n\). Certify \(\overline\varepsilon_n\ge\varepsilon_n\) by checking it against the upper endpoint returned by \(\mathfrak o_\varepsilon\). Cover the optimized covariance domain by a rational symmetric-matrix box, discard only boxes whose disjointness from \(v_{\min}I_d\preceq V\preceq v_{\max}I_d\) has a directed-rounding certificate, and retain every undecided box in the outer cover used for the least-favorable optimization.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak C\)
definitions.construction: Record the rational output \(q^+\), the six rational ledger bounds, finite rational partitions \(\mathcal P_t,\mathcal P_h,\mathcal P_V,\mathcal P_z\), outward intervals \(\mathcal I_G\) for every evaluation of \(G\), outward intervals \(\mathcal I_\phi\) with rational range-reduction and Taylor-remainder witnesses for every Gaussian density or elementary-function bound, and the rational lower bound \(L_{\mathrm{CDF}}\) for \(\inf_{h\in\mathcal H,V\in\mathcal K_V}P\{S(h,Z_V)\le q^++\omega_t+\omega_h+\omega_V\}\) after subtraction of all probability-ledger upper bounds. Also record the rational upper radius \(B_\gamma^+\) and a branch bit. A verifier using exact rational arithmetic checks partition coverage, every directed-rounding inclusion, \(\omega_t+\omega_h+\omega_V\le\zeta\), \(\omega_{\mathrm{tail}}+\omega_{\mathrm{int}}+\omega_{\mathrm{fp}}\le\gamma\), and either \(L_{\mathrm{CDF}}\ge1-\alpha+\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}\) on the refined branch or \(q^+\ge2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\) together with the outward-certified inequality \(2d\exp\{-(B_\gamma^+)^2/(2v_{\max})\}\le\alpha-\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}-\gamma\) on the fallback branch.

definitions.name: \(\mathsf A\)
definitions.construction: Read only \(\mathfrak R\). Compute the outward rational upper radius \(B_\gamma^+\) and the fallback \(2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\). Enumerate the \(K^J\) hard maximizing cells and run at most \(w_{\max}\) best-first subdivisions of \([0,1]\), \(\mathcal H\), \(\mathcal K_V\), and \([-B_\gamma^+,B_\gamma^+]^d\). All arithmetic, exponentials, logarithms, eigenvalue tests, evaluations of \(G\), and Gaussian probability integrations return outward intervals with rational witnesses. Emit the first refined \(q^+\) whose certificate verifies the target lower CDF; if no such certificate closes within the budget, emit the fallback certificate. The algorithm performs at most \(N_{\mathsf A}\) certified box operations and interval-oracle calls, each at precision at most \(m_{\mathsf A}\), and therefore halts on every valid effective input.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{AC}}\)
definitions.construction: Stratify by all benchmark-weighted hard maximizing sets, isolate Gaussian decision-boundary slabs, cover the smooth interior in temperature, and apply coarea or Gaussian polynomial small-ball arguments to the target modulus \(A\) on each remaining stratum.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \((P_n)\in\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)\), the feasible finite-cell estimator satisfies \(d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L(E_n),N(0,V_n)\}\le r_n=C_{\mathrm{BE}}n^{-1/2}\), where \(C_{\mathrm{BE}}\) is an explicit function of \((J,K,p_{\min},e_{\min},B_Y,v_{\min},v_{\max})\); the proof must include the exponentially small empty-cell event and the Hájek-ratio linearization.
statements.justification: This lemma derives the declared Gaussian envelope from primitive finite-cell randomization rather than assuming a property of a named estimator.
statements.gap: CCK gives abstract empirical-process coupling, while no cited result records this uniform finite-cell ratio constant for the present stacked contrasts.
statements.consumer: It supplies a checkable approximation input for the path theorem and for the conditional three-arm illustration.

statements.statement: For every \(c>0\), positive \(b\), and \(u,z\in\mathbb R^K\), \(\ell_{c,b}(u,z)=c\,\mathrm{KL}\{q_{c,b}(u+z)\|q_{c,b}(u)\}\) and \(\ell_{c,b}(u,z)=c^{-1}\int_0^1s\,z^{\top}C\{q_{c,b}(u+sz)\}z\,ds\). Consequently, \(0\le\ell_{c,b}(u,z)\le\operatorname{osc}(z)\) and \(0\le c\ell_{c,b}(u,z)\le\operatorname{osc}(z)^2/8\).
statements.justification: The exact identity fixes the regret normalization and provides an integrable envelope uniformly over temperature.
statements.gap: Fang--Ridder--Xie uses second-order regret at a fixed smooth optimum; the exact categorical identity over the complete temperature scale is not its theorem.
statements.consumer: The path coupling and certified tail truncation both use the global oscillation bounds.

statements.statement: For every \(c>0\) and \(t=c/(1+c)\), the causal penalized-welfare regret satisfies \((1+c)\sqrt n\,\mathscr R_n(c)=G(u_n,E_n)(t)=T_n(t)\). Thus the interior process is an identified causal regret curve, and its values at \(t=0\) and \(t=1\) are defined by the two compactified limits.
statements.justification: This identity prevents the Gaussian path from becoming a detached statistical surrogate and pins every interior coordinate to the planner's causal objective.
statements.gap: The presolve algebra and Fang--Ridder--Xie fixed-weight criterion motivate the identity, but the full local normalization and endpoint compactification are not a published result.
statements.consumer: The simultaneous band can be interpreted directly in penalized-welfare units at every interior temperature selected measurably from the observed sample or the plug-in frontier.

statements.statement: Uniformly for bounded \(u,z\), \(\left|c\ell_{c,b}(u,z)-\frac12z^{\top}C(b)z\right|\le3\|z\|_\infty^2(\|u\|_\infty+\|z\|_\infty)/c\), and \(R^{\top}C(b)R\succeq\beta^2I_{K-1}\). Hence \(G(u,z)(t)\to G(u,z)(1)\) as \(t\uparrow1\) with a computable endpoint modulus.
statements.justification: The projected quadratic endpoint is the fixed-positive-penalty regime after local compactification.
statements.gap: The fixed-penalty quadratic law in Fang--Ridder--Xie does not prove uniform matching to all vanishing local penalties.
statements.consumer: The endpoint reduction connects the path to published regret theory and removes an infinite temperature tail from numerical integration.

statements.statement: Let \(\gamma(v)\) be the gap from \(\max_av_a\) to the largest nonmaximal coordinate, with \(\gamma(v)=\infty\) if every coordinate ties. Then \(\|q_{c,b}(v)-q_{0,b}(v)\|_1\le2\beta^{-1}\exp\{-\gamma(v)/c\}\) and \(|\ell_{c,b}(u,z)-\ell_{0,b}(u,z)|\le2c\log(1/\beta)+2\|z\|_\infty\beta^{-1}\exp\{-\gamma(u+z)/c\}\). Moreover, uniformly in \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(V\in\mathcal K_V\), the probability that any pair of augmented action coordinates of \(R(h+Z_V)\) lies within \(a>0\) is at most \(JK(K-1)a/\sqrt{2\pi v_{\min}}\).
statements.justification: This lemma handles exact and multiway ties without imposing a unique best action.
statements.gap: Whitehouse et al. use uniform weights over exact maximizers for a scalar optimal-value influence function; the present endpoint instead renormalizes the benchmark lottery and requires a uniform multiaction slab bound.
statements.consumer: It controls the discontinuous state geometry in the path coupling and certifies off-grid behavior near the hard rule.

statements.statement: The map \((u,z)\mapsto G(u,z)\) is Borel measurable into \(C([0,1])\); for every \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(V\in\mathcal K_V\), \(S(h,Z_V)\) is finite almost surely; and \((h,V)\mapsto\mathcal L\{S(h,Z_V)\}\) is weakly continuous at every continuity set after the benchmark-weighted tie convention is imposed. Consequently, \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\) is finite and its right-quantile definition is coverage-valid.
statements.justification: Measurability, finiteness, and parameter continuity are required before least-favorable quantile inversion is mathematically meaningful.
statements.gap: Generic continuous mapping does not apply across the hard state discontinuities; the result must use their Gaussian null sets and the explicit endpoint bounds.
statements.consumer: The calibrated critical value is a well-defined functional over the complete local-parameter and covariance envelopes.

statements.statement: The plug-in frontier \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\) is a \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable random element of \(C([0,1])\) and is computable from \(\{(X_{ni},A_{ni},Y_{ni}):1\le i\le n\}\), \(b\), and the declared finite-cell estimators, without \(\Delta_n\), \(u_n\), or \(E_n\). For every \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable \(\widehat t_n\) and every real \(x\), the deterministic inclusion \(\{\sup_{t\in[0,1]}T_n(t)\le x\}\subseteq\{T_n(\widehat t_n)\le x\}\) holds. On \(0<\widehat t_n<1\), with \(\widehat c_n=\widehat t_n/(1-\widehat t_n)\), \(T_n(\widehat t_n)=(1+\widehat c_n)\sqrt n\,\mathscr R_n(\widehat c_n)\). Thus a uniform law or simultaneous coverage bound for the oracle path transfers exactly to a selector computed from the plug-in frontier; no approximation of the unobserved regret by \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\) is required.
statements.justification: The lemma separates the observable frontier used to choose a temperature from the oracle regret path that the confidence envelope covers.
statements.gap: Post-search arguments such as Kang's assume an observed indexed statistic, while the causal regret here contains an unobserved oracle comparator; the exact event inclusion supplies the needed operational bridge without a false plug-in equality.
statements.consumer: A planner can compute a temperature from the displayed plug-in frontier and invoke the simultaneous oracle-regret certificate at precisely that observed-data choice.

statements.statement: There is an explicit computable \(C_{\mathrm{map}}\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly over \((P_n)\in\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)\), \(d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L(T_n),\mathcal L(G(h,Z_{V_n}))\}\le\varepsilon_n\) in \(C([0,1])\), with \(\varepsilon_n\) given in \(\mathrm{def:curve\mbox{-}rate}\) and \(\varepsilon_n\to0\). The same coupling is joint with \(E_n\), and the bound includes both compactified endpoints.
statements.justification: A quantitative function-valued law is the inferential object needed when the KL weight is selected after observing the sample-computable plug-in frontier.
statements.gap: Fang--Ridder--Xie is pointwise at each fixed positive penalty and separate at the deterministic boundary; Whitehouse et al. use one predetermined diverging smoother for a different scalar target.
statements.consumer: Together with the operational-selector bridge, it permits simultaneous regret inference at every temperature chosen measurably from the observed sample or its plug-in frontier.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathfrak R\) be a valid effective input with rational \(\alpha,\gamma,\zeta,\overline\varepsilon_n\), total interval oracles for \(p,b,v_{\min},v_{\max},p_{\min},\beta,\varepsilon_n\), rational-box representations of every optimized \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(V\in\mathcal K_V\), and \(\varepsilon_n\le\overline\varepsilon_n\) with \(\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}+\gamma<\alpha\). The algorithm \(\mathsf A(\mathfrak R)\) halts after at most \(N_{\mathsf A}\) certified box operations and oracle calls of precision at most \(m_{\mathsf A}\), and returns \((Q^+_{n,\alpha},\mathcal E_n,\mathfrak C)\). An exact-rational verifier accepts \(\mathfrak C\) only after checking every elementary-function, spectral, path, and Gaussian-probability outward enclosure, the inequalities \(\omega_t+\omega_h+\omega_V\le\zeta\) and \(\omega_{\mathrm{tail}}+\omega_{\mathrm{int}}+\omega_{\mathrm{fp}}\le\gamma\), and the branch-specific rational conditions in the calibration-certificate definition. Every accepted certificate implies \(\inf_{h\in\mathcal H,V\in\mathcal K_V}P\{S(h,Z_V)\le Q^+_{n,\alpha}+\zeta\}\ge1-\alpha+\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}\). This implication is valid for the refined branch and for the rational fallback \(Q^+_{n,\alpha}=2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\), including when the least-favorable law has atoms. Counting each interval primitive at unit cost, the bit complexity is polynomial in \(N_{\mathsf A}\), the maximum input bit length, and the oracle-output bit length at \(m_{\mathsf A}\).
statements.justification: A critical value is operationally honest only when its real inputs have effective names, its rounding direction can be checked independently, and its worst-case running time is finite.
statements.gap: Genz and Miwa supply integration engines for supplied rectangles or orthants, and Wang--Kennedy self-validates rectangular probabilities; none proves termination for this nonlinear continuum event or least-favorable parameter envelope.
statements.consumer: The algorithm turns the asymptotic path law into an auditable critical value for low-dimensional multiaction experiments.

statements.statement: For any sequence of accepted effective certificates with \(\varepsilon_n\le\overline\varepsilon_n\to0\), let \(C_{n,\alpha}=Q^+_{n,\alpha}+\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}+\zeta\). Then \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)}P_n\{T_n(t)\le C_{n,\alpha}\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\}\ge1-\alpha\). For every operational selector \(\widehat t_n\) that is \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable, including every Borel-measurable choice based on \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)}P_n\{T_n(\widehat t_n)\le C_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\). At an interior selected value this event is exactly \(\{(1+\widehat c_n)\sqrt n\,\mathscr R_n(\widehat c_n)\le C_{n,\alpha}\}\), where \(\widehat c_n=\widehat t_n/(1-\widehat t_n)\). The plug-in frontier is used only to generate the observed-data selector; coverage concerns the oracle normalized regret path. The conclusion uses one-sided ramps and the verified lower CDF bracket and does not assume continuity of the distribution of \(S(h,Z_V)\).
statements.justification: This is the operational selection-valid coverage theorem: the selected temperature is computed from observed data, while the covered quantity is the oracle causal regret, and validity remains correct at exact ties and quantile atoms.
statements.gap: CCK and Giessing anti-concentration results apply to Gaussian-process suprema, Fang--Santos quantile validity requires regularity not supplied at atoms, and none states the observed-selector-to-oracle-regret bridge for a nonlinear causal frontier.
statements.consumer: A planner may inspect the sample-computable welfare--divergence frontier, choose a temperature measurably from it, and report a certified upper bound for the oracle regret at that chosen point.

statements.statement: In the binary one-stratum submodel with \(\mathcal H=\{0\}\), \(b=(1/2,1/2)\), and scalar \(V\in(v_{\min},v_{\max})\), let \(q_{1-\alpha}(V)\) be the right \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(S(0,Z_V)\). There exist \(c_1,c_2,s_0>0\) such that \(c_1s\le q_{1-\alpha}(V)-q_{1-\alpha}(V-s)\le c_2s\) for \(0<s<s_0\). Hence a localized plug-in calibration that may underestimate \(V\) by \(s\) cannot be made uniformly honest with \(o(s)\) critical-value inflation.
statements.justification: The result certifies the order of the covariance component when a user replaces the robust spectral envelope by localized plug-in calibration.
statements.gap: CCK compares maxima under covariance perturbations, and Fang--Ridder--Xie links covariance to fixed-weight regret; neither gives the sharp quantile sensitivity of this nonlinear path supremum.
statements.consumer: Implementers learn when the robust envelope can be localized and how much critical-value inflation a covariance undershoot necessarily costs.

statements.statement: Using the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{AC}}\), characterize every atom of \(S(h,Z_V)\) generated by flat hard-max strata and determine whether there exists a computable \(A(x)\downarrow0\) such that, uniformly over \(h\in\mathcal H\), \(V\in\mathcal K_V\), and \(q\in\mathbb R\), the probability of \(q<S(h,Z_V)\le q+x\) after removing the enumerated atom at \(q\) is at most \(A(x)\). If so, use it to make the algorithm return a two-sided least-favorable quantile bracket of prescribed value width.
statements.justification: This is the genuinely open probability-theoretic step separating an honest conservative certificate from sharp quantile computation.
statements.gap: CCK and Giessing prove concentration bounds for suprema of Gaussian coordinates or processes, not for the supremum of the nonlinear compactified Bregman path with flat hard cells.
statements.consumer: A sharp modulus would bound excess conservativeness and certify the numerical distance to the ideal least-favorable critical value.

sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. randomized experiment with fixed finite stratum set \(\mathcal J\), fixed finite action set \(\mathcal A\), and known action probabilities \(e_{ja}\).
sampling_model.units: For each local row \(n\), the full units \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_n\), while the planner observes only \(O^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ni}=(X_{ni},A_{ni},Y_{ni})\) and hence only \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditional randomization satisfies \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}\perp A\mid X\), consistency, and \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every stratum has \(p_j\ge p_{\min}\), every randomized action has \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\), and every benchmark action has \(b_{ja}\ge\beta\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite randomized cells are estimated by within-cell Hájek means and stratum masses by empirical frequencies. These observed estimators generate \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\), the only frontier supplied to the temperature selector. The Gaussian approximation envelope for the distinct oracle regret path is derived from bounded outcomes, cell mass, and overlap in \(\mathrm{lem:cell\mbox{-}gaussian}\), rather than assumed for the estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed positive \(\lambda\), \(nR_\lambda(\widehat\theta)\) converges to one-half of a Gaussian quadratic form.
A predetermined diverging inverse temperature yields root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity for the unsmoothed optimal-policy value.
Convergent binary treatment rules are represented by rules in a shifted Gaussian limit experiment.
A scalar empirical-process supremum is coupled nonasymptotically to the corresponding Gaussian supremum.
The concentration function of a standardized Gaussian-process supremum is bounded by its expected supremum.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian limit is equivalent to full differentiability of the transformation.
Gaussian-vector maxima admit covariance comparison and anti-concentration bounds under arbitrary correlation.
A separation-of-variables transformation reduces Gaussian rectangle probabilities to bounded multiple integration.
Taylor expansion, interval analysis, and automatic differentiation self-validate Gaussian rectangle probabilities.
Recursive integration evaluates noncentered Gaussian orthant probabilities for positive-definite correlation matrices.
Joint Gaussian critical values give coverage after selecting a series dimension from the searched specification set.

tldr: A finite-stratum randomized lottery generates a continuum of benchmark-centered Gibbs rules indexed by a KL penalty. The normalized oracle-minus-estimated regret is compactified into one continuous path whose hard endpoint uses benchmark weights on every maximizing set and whose high-penalty endpoint is a projected categorical-covariance quadratic form. The main result is a quantitative uniform Gaussian approximation for this entire nonlinear path. An observed plug-in welfare frontier, computed only from cell estimates and empirical stratum weights, supplies the operational temperature selector, while a deterministic simultaneous-event bridge transfers coverage to the oracle regret at that selected temperature. An effective interval-and-Gaussian-integration algorithm takes rational data or named interval oracles, emits a machine-checkable directed-rounding certificate within an explicit work bound, and falls back to a finite analytic Gaussian-tail certificate when adaptive integration does not close. The resulting atom-safe envelope is valid after every observed-data-measurable temperature choice. Sharp anti-concentration of the nonlinear Gaussian supremum remains an explicit open question rather than an assumption.

project_justification.gap: Fixed positive KL penalties have a quadratic regret law, while the hard assignment boundary and softmax inference for one predetermined smoothing sequence are studied separately. No published result gives a quantitative joint law or a certified critical value over the full penalty menu.
project_justification.niche: Finite multiaction lotteries create a tractable but nonstandard function-valued statistic: its interior coordinates are nonlinear Gaussian transforms, its hard endpoint is directionally differentiable with benchmark-weighted multiway ties, and its opposite endpoint has a different quadratic normalization.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the primitive finite-cell Gaussian certificate, matches both endpoints, proves an explicit tie-slab coupling rate in \(C([0,1])\), defines a sample-computable plug-in frontier and its observed-data sigma-field, and turns a one-sided lower CDF bracket with effective input names, directed rounding, a checkable output witness, and a finite fallback bound into computably honest inference after an operational frontier-based temperature choice without assuming away atoms.

related_work: Fang--Ridder--Xie studies benchmark-centered KL assignment and proves a quadratic regret limit for each fixed positive penalty; its Conclusion leaves data-driven penalty choice open, and its deterministic binary analysis is separate. The finite-cell dummy-feature inclusion in that framework and the equality of the \(t=1\) quadratic formula with its fixed-penalty specialization are used only as sanity and reduction checks, not as contributions or claimed extensions. Its three-arm commitment-savings frontier motivates an illustration, but no finite-stratification adequacy claim is made. Whitehouse--Chen--Austern--Syrgkanis uses softmax smoothing to estimate one unsmoothed optimal-policy value along a predetermined diverging temperature and permits exact ties, but its uniform tie weights and scalar target differ from the benchmark-weighted regret path. Hirano--Porter supplies the shifted-Gaussian local decision experiment for binary hard treatment choice, not a multiaction path law. Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato supplies finite-net Gaussian coupling and anti-concentration for suprema of Gaussian processes; those results inform the proof, but \(G(h,Z_V)\) is nonlinear in \(Z_V\) and is not itself a Gaussian process. Fang--Santos identifies the directional derivative and bootstrap issue at max-type boundaries, while its quantile conclusions do not provide certified atom-safe continuum calibration here. Genz, Wang--Kennedy, and Miwa--Hayter--Kuriki provide Gaussian rectangle or orthant integration components; their algorithms do not reduce or certify the proposed nonlinear continuum sublevel event. Kang supplies the logic that a simultaneous band survives a tuning choice computed from an observed linear series path; it does not distinguish a sample-computable selection frontier from an unobserved oracle regret target or cover the changing endpoint geometry and numerical certification here.
technical_internal_limitation: The one-sided algorithm terminates and certifies coverage because the work-capped refinement has an analytic Gaussian-tail fallback, but it need not return a critical value within a prescribed numerical distance of \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\). Without the open concentration modulus or exact enumeration of every flat stratum, ambiguous boundary boxes can encode an atom and prevent a two-sided value-width certificate. The rational fallback \(2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\) can be conservative.
honest_scope: The theorem is uniform only for fixed \(J\) and \(K\), positive benchmark probabilities, positive stratum and treatment probabilities, bounded outcomes, compact local contrasts, and a covariance spectrum bounded away from zero. It excludes boundary benchmarks, singular covariance, growing action or stratum counts, disappearing cells, and continuous covariates without a prespecified finite stratification. The finite-cell embedding in Fang--Ridder--Xie and the \(t=1\) fixed-penalty quadratic equality are sanity and reduction checks only. The commitment-savings display is an illustration conditional on prespecified cells. Temperature selection is restricted to \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable rules, including rules based on the displayed plug-in frontier; the plug-in frontier is not claimed to estimate the unobserved oracle regret path. The basic simultaneous upper envelope for the oracle path and its exact transfer to these operational selectors are the settled targets to prove; a sharp small-interval modulus and a two-sided quantile-accuracy guarantee are open.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The source TeX and HTML were read at the Introduction, Sections \(2.1\), \(2.2\), and \(3\), Theorems 1, 2, and 6, the proofs of Theorems 1 and 2, Section \(7\), and the Conclusion. Theorem 2 obtains the fixed-positive-penalty quadratic regret law by a second-order Taylor expansion at an interior optimum; the Conclusion identifies data-driven penalty choice as open.
seed_details.question: Can the locally normalized causal-lottery regret process be coupled uniformly in \(C([0,1])\) to one nonlinear Gaussian path that has the benchmark-weighted hard rule at \(t=0\) and the categorical-covariance quadratic form at \(t=1\)?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The pointwise Taylor expansion in the proof of Fang--Ridder--Xie Theorem 2 ceases to be uniform when \(\lambda\downarrow0\); the optimizer reaches a max-type boundary, while fixed positive \(\lambda\) appears at the opposite compactified endpoint after a different normalization.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for the exact pairs \(\text{KL regret}+\text{temperature path}+\text{simultaneous inference}\) and \(\text{Gibbs-to-hard}+C([0,1])+\text{causal regret}\) found no theorem occupying this path law.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Fang--Ridder--Xie Theorem 2 by making its penalty index uniform.
seed_details.rebuttal: That theorem requires a fixed positive penalty and an interior twice-differentiable optimum; it supplies neither endpoint transition, a path coupling, nor a tie-stable hard derivative.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.1, Theorem 3.1, and the proof of Theorem 2.1 were read. The anti-concentration inequality concerns suprema of standardized Gaussian processes and upgrades Gaussian coupling to honest adaptive bands.
seed_details.question: Can a one-sided ramp and certified lower CDF brackets yield nominal simultaneous coverage for \(\sup_tG(h,Z_V)(t)\) at every atom, without assuming a concentration density for this nonlinear Gaussian functional?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The CCK coupling-to-coverage step invokes anti-concentration of a Gaussian-process supremum; here the temperature coordinates are nonlinear functions of one Gaussian vector, so the Gaussian-process premise fails before quantile inversion.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for atom-safe critical values for nonlinear Gaussian suprema and for nonlinear Bregman-path anti-concentration found Gaussian-max results but no Gibbs-regret result.
seed_details.red_team: A positive critical-value shift is a routine Portmanteau argument and therefore not a contribution.
seed_details.rebuttal: The ramp inequality alone is elementary, but its uniform least-favorable implementation, exact atom convention, computable error ledger, and observed-data-selector-valid causal envelope are absent from the comparator literature and form a theorem only when coupled to the quantitative path law and operational bridge.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The journal abstract and scope were opened, and the authors' accessible proceedings derivation was read through its setup, recursive orthoscheme integration formulas, factorial decomposition construction, and closing scope discussion. The method evaluates supplied noncentered Gaussian orthants under positive-definite correlation; it does not treat continuum intersections of curved regret inequalities.
seed_details.question: Can interval evaluation, endpoint moduli, Gaussian tail truncation, and adaptive cell integration produce a terminating one-sided certificate for the least-favorable continuum-temperature critical value?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first new numerical step is to replace a Gaussian rectangle by rigorous inner and outer finite unions for \(\{z:\sup_tG(h,z)(t)\le q\}\), with separate hard-cell and smooth-interior enclosures.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining certified Gaussian integration with softmax, Bregman sublevel sets, and continuum temperature returned only generic interval quadrature or rectangle-probability algorithms.
seed_details.red_team: This is only an implementation of classical multivariate-normal integration.
seed_details.rebuttal: Classical routines integrate fixed rectangles or orthants; the proposed termination theorem must certify temperature, local-parameter, covariance, tail, and curved-region errors and remain valid at hard-endpoint atoms.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorems 1--3, and their Slepian-interpolation proofs were read. The soft maximum is a proof smoother for maxima of linear Gaussian coordinates; the theorem does not compare nonlinear KL-regret paths.
seed_details.question: Can Slepian covariance interpolation and hard-tie slabs yield a computable one-sided law comparison for \(\sup_tG(h,Z_V)(t)\) over a spectral covariance envelope?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The interpolation derivative now contains the Hessian of the discretized nonlinear regret supremum rather than the categorical Hessian of a log-sum-exp approximation to a linear maximum.
seed_details.destination_search: The pair \(\text{Gaussian covariance comparison}+\text{nonlinear Gibbs regret}\) was not occupied; nearby results cover linear maxima and Gaussian-process suprema.
seed_details.red_team: CCK covariance comparison already allows arbitrary covariance, so plug-in robustness is immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Arbitrary covariance in CCK refers to maxima of Gaussian coordinates; it does not supply derivative bounds across the hard-tie partition or the projected quadratic endpoint of this nonlinear functional.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Section \(7\), Figure 2, and the Conclusion were read. The application fixes \(c=1\) as a preference value, reports a prespecified frontier for the three-arm benchmark \((0.25,0.50,0.25)\), and calls the comparison descriptive.
seed_details.question: Can the three-arm commitment-savings plug-in frontier carry an upper oracle-regret certificate after any observed-data-measurable choice of its displayed KL weight, including choices approaching deterministic assignment?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Pointwise bootstrap standard errors must be replaced by a joint oracle-path approximation and an exact event bridge from the observed plug-in frontier selector, with the derivative changing at the hard endpoint.
seed_details.destination_search: Kang2019 supplies post-search coverage for approximately linear observed series statistics over tuning specifications, but no search result covered selection from a nonlinear causal plug-in frontier with coverage of its distinct oracle-regret path and hard max endpoint.
seed_details.red_team: A simultaneous band over a displayed finite grid already solves the empirical problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: A finite displayed grid does not cover an observed-data continuum choice or temperatures converging to either compactified endpoint; the missing off-grid modulus and the observed-selector-to-oracle-path bridge are the mathematical content.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, near-tie bias lemma, Theorem 3.3, its orthogonal-score proof, and the Conclusion were read. The paper gives a scalar asymptotically linear estimator for a predetermined diverging inverse temperature and leaves adaptive temperature selection and efficiency under ties open.
seed_details.question: Is there a semiparametric efficiency bound for regret evaluated at an unrestricted observed-data-measurable selected temperature when exact ties have positive probability?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The pathwise derivative would have to pass through the random selector and the multi-valued hard maximizer, rather than through one predetermined softmax score.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches located efficiency theory for fixed smooth rules and scalar smoothed optimal values, but not for an unrestricted observed-data-selector-indexed regret functional.
seed_details.red_team: The selected-temperature target is not regular, so a classical efficiency bound need not exist.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds even for an unrestricted observed-data-measurable selector, and no defensible regular parameter was found without changing the target.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Proposition 3.1, Theorems 3.2, 3.4, and 3.5, the semiparametric analogues, and the final example were read. The paper reduces binary treatment choice to a shifted Gaussian limit experiment and derives Bayes and minimax cutoff rules.
seed_details.question: What is the minimax sup-norm estimation rate for the entire local Gibbs-to-hard regret curve over compact local alternatives?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The Hirano--Porter one-dimensional slice and cutoff complete-class argument would need a loss on a multiaction function-valued regret target, not binary decision loss.
seed_details.destination_search: No direct minimax path-estimation result was found, but the fixed finite dimension makes a parametric lower bound likely and does not expose a new regime frontier.
seed_details.red_team: The rate is the ordinary finite-dimensional parametric rate after a Lipschitz transformation away from ties.
seed_details.rebuttal: Near ties destroy global Lipschitz continuity, but the available substrate did not reveal a nontrivial matched rate distinct from the coupling modulus.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, best-in-class regret definition, Theorem 2, Section \(7\), and the Conclusion were read. Their penalty is a planner preference and is deliberately not optimized from prediction loss.
seed_details.question: Can a data-chosen temperature rule satisfy an oracle inequality for causal welfare regret relative to the best temperature in the compactified menu?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The planner-preference interpretation makes welfare values at different temperatures different objectives, so empirical welfare maximization across temperatures lacks one coherent oracle target.
seed_details.destination_search: Policy-learning papers give regret to the best policy under one welfare criterion; no source supplied a defensible oracle ordering across different KL preferences.
seed_details.red_team: The oracle comparison is normatively ill-posed because changing temperature changes the planner's objective.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds unless a common external welfare-minus-constraint criterion is added, which would materially change the assigned topic.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The experiment design, treatment arms, main savings effects, robustness discussion, and conclusion were read. The known randomization supports exact tests for sharp nulls, not direct observation of every unit's regret curve.
seed_details.question: Can randomization or conformal inversion produce an exact finite-sample simultaneous confidence envelope for the Gibbs-to-hard regret frontier?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: An exact permutation orbit would require an imputable sharp-null schedule for all potential outcomes entering every candidate lottery value.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found exact randomization inference for sharp nulls but no exact finite-sample inversion for this composite missing-potential-outcome regret curve.
seed_details.red_team: The regret frontier is not sharp-null imputable, so treatment permutations do not preserve the required statistic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the desired composite frontier; imposing constant effects would make the result too narrow.

literature_map.settled: For each fixed positive KL weight, the best smooth rule is regular and its \(n\)-scaled regret has a Gaussian quadratic-form limit; the unpenalized binary case is treated separately through a welfare-process bound.
literature_map.open_boundary: No joint normalized law spans vanishing, fixed, and diverging local penalties, and the paper explicitly leaves data-driven weight choice open.

literature_map.settled: A predetermined diverging inverse temperature can deliver scalar root-\(n\) inference for an unsmoothed optimal-policy value; directional delta and derivative-aware bootstrap methods handle fixed max-type maps.
literature_map.open_boundary: Neither source supplies a quantitative full-temperature regret-path law, benchmark-weighted hard ties, or critical values valid at atoms after selection from an observed plug-in frontier.

literature_map.settled: Finite nets and oscillation bounds couple empirical-process suprema to Gaussian suprema, and separable Gaussian-process suprema have explicit concentration-function bounds.
literature_map.open_boundary: The coordinates \(G(h,Z_V)(t)\) are nonlinear in one Gaussian vector and are not a Gaussian process; hard cells may create atoms.

literature_map.settled: Maxima of linear Gaussian coordinates admit covariance comparison under arbitrary correlation, and strong variance can replace coordinatewise variance for Gaussian-process suprema.
literature_map.open_boundary: No theorem compares the nonlinear KL/Bregman regret supremum through covariance perturbations across its hard and projected-quadratic endpoints.

literature_map.settled: Conditional transformations, recursive orthant integration, and interval Taylor enclosures compute or certify Gaussian rectangle and orthant probabilities.
literature_map.open_boundary: A continuum intersection of curved softmax inequalities with hard argmax cells and least-favorable parameter optimization is outside those algorithms.

literature_map.settled: Joint Gaussian critical values protect inference after series-dimension search, while the causal-lottery application reports a prespecified weight grid.
literature_map.open_boundary: The observed-data-measurable nonlinear continuum-temperature selector, its distinct oracle-regret target, and its two changing endpoints are not covered.

literature_map.settled: Binary hard treatment choice under local alternatives reduces to a shifted Gaussian limit experiment with Bayes and minimax cutoff rules.
literature_map.open_boundary: The source does not state a multiaction Gibbs/KL path law or simultaneous pathwise calibration.
